PPTI Research Publication Trends and Strategic Positioning

A bibliometric report on recent PPTI publication activity, journal distribution, citation visibility, open-access status, and research themes.

Oct 1, 2026, 12:35 PM UTC

Abstract

This report examines 559Source for 559Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications distinct Scopus-indexed publications associated with 64Source for 64Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications PPTI researchers during the 24Source for 24Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications-month period from 1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications October 2024 to 30Source for 30Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications September 2026. The publications appeared in 314Source for 314Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications journals and had received 2,543Source for 2,543Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications citations at the time of data collection. The analysis considers publication activity, journal concentration, citation visibility, open-access status, and recurring author keywords to describe the institution's recent research profile. The results show a broad journal portfolio, with the ten most frequently used titles accounting for 20%Source for 20%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publications. International Journal of Biological Macromolecules was the most frequently used journal, with 22Source for 22Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications articles, while Fermentation was the most prevalent normalized author keyword, appearing in 14Source for 14Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications publications. Open-access articles represented 43%Source for 43%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of the portfolio. Journals below the established tier accounted for 73%Source for 73%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publications, while developing and exploratory keywords accounted for 89%Source for 89%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publication–keyword associations. Compared with the August 2026 edition, the rolling portfolio contained 13 more distinct publications; its cumulative citation total was 251Source for 251Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications higher and the open-access share moved +1.0Source for +1.0Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications percentage points. Together, these findings provide an evidence base for understanding PPTI's publication patterns and for aligning future manuscripts with demonstrated areas of research activity and journal experience.

1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications. Scope and method

The report is based on Scopus publication records associated with PPTI researchers and dated between 1Source for 1Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications October 2024 to 30Source for 30Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications September 2026. The unit of analysis is a distinct Scopus-indexed publication rather than an author–publication record; consequently, a publication co-authored by more than one PPTI researcher is counted once in the portfolio totals. Citation values represent the cumulative Scopus counts available when the dataset was collected, and thematic analysis is based on normalized author keywords. Monthly commentary is generated by comparing the current metrics and rankings with the preceding saved edition under the same methodology. Journal and keyword frequencies therefore describe both the present portfolio and any material movement since the previous report.

3.3Source for 3.3Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications Publication frequency and citation visibility

The journal map relates the number of distinct publications in each outlet to their cumulative citation totals. Journals positioned toward the upper right combine repeated PPTI publication activity with comparatively strong citation visibility. In contrast, a journal with high citation counts but few publications may reflect the influence of a small number of articles. The two measures are therefore presented as complementary dimensions of the portfolio: frequency indicates the extent of recent use, whereas citations indicate the visibility accumulated by the articles published in that outlet.

5Source for 5Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications. Conclusion

PPTI's recent Scopus-indexed output is characterized by sustained publication activity, a broad journal base, and identifiable concentrations of research expertise. Across 559Source for 559Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications distinct publications, the portfolio combines repeated use of established outlets with dissemination across 314Source for 314Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications journals, while 43%Source for 43%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of articles were available through open access. The tier analysis shows that 73%Source for 73%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publications occurred in developing or exploratory journals and that 89%Source for 89%Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications of publication–keyword associations sat outside the established keyword tier. Compared with the August 2026 edition, the rolling portfolio contained 13 more distinct publications; its cumulative citation total was 251Source for 251Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications higher and the open-access share moved +1.0Source for +1.0Source: Scopus publication snapshotTable: scopus_publications percentage points. The journal and keyword results together document the institution's recent publication position and provide a reproducible baseline against which subsequent reporting periods can be compared.
